titre: The deepest canyon in the world is not the Grand Canyon
accroche: In Tibet, a river carves a gorge nearly three times deeper than the Grand Canyon, and almost no one had kayaked it before 2002.
contenu_vulgarise:
The Grand Canyon in Arizona, carved by the Colorado River, is arguably the most photographed canyon in the world: about 1,800 meters deep at its lowest point. Yet it falls well short of a far lesser-known canyon: that of the Yarlung Tsangpo, in Tibet, where the river plunges in places to more than 5,300 meters, according to NASA, nearly three times deeper. Wikipedia cites an estimate of up to 6,009 meters at the deepest point.

## The Mechanism

The Yarlung Tsangpo rises near Mount Kailash in western Tibet, then crosses the Tibetan Plateau for nearly 3,000 km before making, at its eastern end, a sharp turn to the south. There, between the peaks of Namcha Barwa (7,782 m) and Gyala Peri, the river has carved its most spectacular gorge, more than 500 km long, according to NASA.

What makes this gorge exceptional is not the river's power alone, but where it sits: around the Namcha Barwa and Gyala Peri massif, geologists have identified what they call a “tectonic aneurysm,” an isolated zone where uplift and exhumation of rock are extreme. Erosion there weakens the crust, which makes deep, hot, ductile rock rise; this rising in turn feeds erosion, in a self-sustaining loop. Dating of the rock exhumed in this massif points to incision of about 3 millimeters per year over the last ten million years. The sources place the canyon's greatest depth in the same spot: between these two peaks, it reaches an average depth of about 5,000 meters. They do not say that this mechanism alone explains the record.

## The Shift

For a long time this canyon was little more than a blank on the maps. Earlier attempts to kayak the upper gorge had ended in tragedy. In 2002, a group of seven people led by filmmaker Scott Lindgren, accompanied by 93 others on the ground, became the first team to kayak it: 45 days on the water, with no maps available for the heart of the gorge, after studying satellite images of every mile of the river.

At the canyon's exit, at the Indian border, the river is already down to just 660 meters in elevation: it then changes its name and becomes the Brahmaputra. So the canyon is not only a depth record: it lies in one of the two zones of the Himalaya, along with Nanga Parbat in the west, where the uplift of rock is extreme.

repere.texte: In places, the Yarlung Tsangpo canyon exceeds 5,300 meters in depth, three times the Grand Canyon, over more than 500 km in length.

carte.punch: The deepest canyon in the world is not in Arizona, but in Tibet.
carte.idee: Where the Yarlung Tsangpo wraps around Mount Namcha Barwa in Tibet, the river has carved a gorge more than 5,300 meters deep in places: nearly three times the Grand Canyon. Its upper gorge was not kayaked until 2002, after 45 days and tragic earlier attempts.

pour_aller_plus_loin.note: Details the discrepancies between the various depth estimates and the full geography of the canyon.

quiz.question: Where does the Yarlung Tsangpo canyon reach its greatest depth, according to the sources?
choix: Near the river's source, at the foot of Mount Kailash in western Tibet
At the Indian border, where the river becomes the Brahmaputra
Between Namcha Barwa and Gyala Peri, in the massif where geologists have spotted a tectonic aneurysm
On the Tibetan Plateau, in the wide open valleys of the river's central stretch
quiz.explication: It is between the peaks of Namcha Barwa and Gyala Peri that the canyon reaches an average depth of about 5,000 meters, and it is also there that geologists have identified a “tectonic aneurysm.” The sources establish this coincidence of place, not a cause-and-effect link. At the Indian border, the river is down to just 660 meters in elevation, and on the plateau it flows through open valleys.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What maximum depth does Wikipedia give for the Yarlung Tsangpo canyon?
choix: About 1,800 meters, the same depth as the Grand Canyon of the Colorado
Up to 6,009 meters, the greatest canyon depth on land according to Wikipedia
About 3,000 meters, twice the Grand Canyon
More than 8,000 meters, the elevation of Mount Namcha Barwa
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Wikipedia gives 6,009 meters at the deepest point, against about 1,857 meters for the Grand Canyon of the Colorado. NASA gives more than 5,300 meters in places.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who led the first kayak descent of the upper gorge of the Yarlung Tsangpo, in 2002?
choix: A group of seven people led by filmmaker Scott Lindgren, accompanied by 93 people on the ground
A lone Tibetan mountaineer, with no logistical support, following NASA maps
A NASA scientific expedition equipped with drones to map the canyon
A Chinese army team, which mapped the canyon before opening a tourist road
quiz_supplementaire.explication: NASA reports that in 2002 seven people led by filmmaker Scott Lindgren became the first team to kayak the upper gorge, with 93 people on the ground, after 45 days on the water.

quiz_supplementaire.question: What does the Yarlung Tsangpo become after crossing the Indian border, at 660 meters in elevation?
choix: It flows directly into the Indian Ocean under its Tibetan name
It joins the Ganges before forming a single delta
It disappears into an underground lake before resurfacing in Bangladesh
It changes its name and becomes the Brahmaputra
quiz_supplementaire.explication: At the Indian border, the river is down to just 660 meters in elevation, then enters Arunachal Pradesh and becomes the Brahmaputra.
